differential.name: Diabetic nephropathy
differential.rationale: Microalbuminuria with longstanding type 2 diabetes and CKD in a hypertensive, obese patient makes diabetic kidney disease the leading cause of his renal impairment.

differential.name: Hypertensive nephrosclerosis
differential.rationale: Persistent essential hypertension contributes to arteriolar nephrosclerosis and can explain the modestly reduced GFR and elevated creatinine.

differential.name: Obesity‑related glomerulopathy
differential.rationale: BMI >30 and metabolic syndrome predispose to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis‑type changes that can coexist with diabetic and hypertensive injury.

differential.name: Anemia of chronic kidney disease
differential.rationale: CKD‑related reduced erythropoietin production accounts for the documented anemia in this patient.

differential.name: NSAID‑induced acute on chronic kidney injury
differential.rationale: Over‑the‑counter NSAID use (common in patients with limited social support) can precipitate a rise in creatinine superimposed on chronic kidney disease.
